helpIntro: The University of Washington uses numeric grades from 4.0 down to 0.7 in 0.1 steps, plus 0.0. Enter UW credits and the exact numeric grade shown on your record.
helpNote: For the standard undergraduate UW GPA. Transfer grades do not enter the UW cumulative GPA. Repeat Impact is unavailable because UW does not use ordinary grade replacement; the first two graded attempts count under the modern repeat rule.
helpExample: A 5-credit course at 3.7 earns 18.5 grade points, and a 5-credit course at 3.0 earns 15.0. Together, 33.5 ÷ 10 = 3.35.

gradeExplanations.S: Satisfactory is excluded from the quarterly and cumulative GPA.
gradeExplanations.NS: Not Satisfactory is excluded from GPA and does not earn credit.
gradeExplanations.NC: No Credit is excluded from GPA.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete is excluded until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.X: Grade not submitted; excluded until a final grade is recorded.
gradeExplanations.HW: Hardship withdrawal is excluded from GPA.
gradeExplanations.RD: Registrar Drop is excluded from GPA.
gradeExplanations.N: N is used for certain multi-quarter courses and is not a numeric GPA grade until final grading is resolved.

specialTypes.name: UW course, standard grading
specialTypes.note: Use the exact numeric grade and UW credits from the record.

specialTypes.name: External transfer course
specialTypes.note: Transfer credit and transfer GPA can matter for admission or program review, but transfer grades do not enter the UW cumulative GPA.

specialTypes.name: Third-or-later repeat attempt
specialTypes.note: Under the modern repeat notation, grades beyond the first repeat are not calculated in GPA; confirm unusual or historical records with the Registrar.

specialTypes.name: Law, Medicine, or Dentistry record
specialTypes.note: These schools have grading exceptions and should not be forced into the standard undergraduate decimal profile.

repeatPolicy.note: For a standard modern repeat, enter the first and second graded attempts as separate completed courses; both count in GPA. Do not use the replacement estimator. Third-or-later repeat grades are not included under the modern transcript rule.
